cues.zh: 校对：Eren Özbay 审核：Denise RQ
cues.en: Transcriber: Eren Özbay Reviewer: Denise RQ

cues.zh: 非常感谢。
cues.en: Thank you very much.

cues.zh: 确实，我出生在一个乐队里；
cues.en: It's true I was born into a band;

cues.zh: 字面意义上的，我是说真的。
cues.en: very literally, I mean that literally.

cues.zh: 我出生时，我的四个哥哥已经在玩音乐了，
cues.en: When I was born, my four older brothers who were already playing music,

cues.zh: 他们知道需要一个贝斯手
cues.en: knew that they needed a bass player

cues.zh: （笑声）
cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.zh: 来凑齐家庭乐队。
cues.en: to round out the family band.

cues.zh: 我生来就担了这个角色。
cues.en: I was born into that role.

cues.zh: 现在我年纪大了，回望过去，现在别人叫我老师。
cues.en: As I'm older I'm looking back right now, now that I'm called a teacher.

cues.zh: 当我回想那段经历，以及我是怎么被教的，
cues.en: When I look back on that, and how I was taught,

cues.zh: 我意识到我其实并没有被教过。
cues.en: I realized that I wasn't really taught.

cues.zh: 所以我说音乐是一门语言；
cues.en: Which is why I say that music is a language;

cues.zh: 因为如果你想想你的母语，
cues.en: because if you think about your first language,

cues.zh: 对我来说，以及在座大多数人可能都是英语，
cues.en: for me, and probably most of us here might be English,

cues.zh: 那我就以英语为例吧。
cues.en: so I'm just going to go with English.

cues.zh: 如果你想想自己是怎么学会它的，你会发现你并不是被教会的。
cues.en: If you think about how you learned it, you realize you weren't taught it.

cues.zh: 刚才有人跟你说话了。
cues.en: People just spoke to you.

cues.zh: 但最妙的地方，也正是有趣之处
cues.en: But the coolest thing is where it gets interesting

cues.zh: 因为你可以回话。
cues.en: because you were allowed to speak back.

cues.zh: 拿音乐来举例，
cues.en: If I take the music example,

cues.zh: 大多数情况下，我们的初学者不能跟水平更高的人一起演奏。
cues.en: in most cases, our beginners are not allowed to play with the better people.

cues.zh: 你被困在初级班。
cues.en: You're stuck in the beginning class.

cues.zh: 你得在那儿待上好几年，
cues.en: You have to remain there a few years,

cues.zh: 直到你被提升到中级，然后是高级；
cues.en: until you are elevated to the intermediate, and then advanced;

cues.zh: 而且就算你从高级班毕业了，
cues.en: and after you graduate the advanced class,

cues.zh: 你还得出去吃很多苦头。
cues.en: you still have to go out and pay a lot of dues.

cues.zh: 但语言不一样，
cues.en: But with language,

cues.zh: 用音乐术语来说，即使还是个婴儿，你也在和专业人士一起“即兴演奏”。
cues.en: to use a musical term, even as a baby you're "jamming" with professionals.

cues.zh: 一直如此。
cues.en: All the time.

cues.zh: 以至于你甚至都不知道自己是个初学者。
cues.en: To the point that you don't even know you're a beginner.

cues.zh: 没人会说：“我不能跟你说话，除非——你得先到那边去。
cues.en: No one says, "I can't talk to you until-- You got to go over there.

cues.zh: 等你大一点了，我才能跟你说话。”
cues.en: When you're older, then I can speak to you."

cues.zh: （笑声）
cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.zh: 这不会发生。
cues.en: That doesn't happen.

cues.zh: 没人告诉你必须说什么。
cues.en: No one tells you what you have to say.

cues.zh: 没人让你坐在角落里练习。
cues.en: You're not made to sit in a corner and practice.

cues.zh: 甚至你说错了，也没人纠正你。
cues.en: You're never even corrected when you're wrong.

cues.zh: 想想看：你两三岁时，一遍又一遍地把一个词说错，
cues.en: Think about it: when you're 2-3 years old, and you say a word wrong over and over,

cues.zh: 没人纠正你。
cues.en: no one corrects you.

cues.zh: 如果你错得够多次，
cues.en: If you say it wrong enough times,

cues.zh: 父母不会纠正你，反而会学你的说法。
cues.en: instead of correcting you, your parents learn your way.

cues.zh: （笑声）
cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.zh: 然后他们也开始说错了！
cues.en: And they start saying it wrong too!

cues.zh: 最酷的是，你始终保持自由，
cues.en: The coolest part of that is that you remain free,

cues.zh: 用你自己的说话方式。
cues.en: with how you talk.

cues.zh: 所以你从来不必遵循那种音乐式的学习路径——
cues.en: And so you never have to follow the musical role of learning

cues.zh: 学这么多年，然后才去寻找自己的声音。
cues.en: all these years and then, going and finding your voice.

cues.zh: 而你的说话声音，你从未失去过。
cues.en: With your speaking voice, you've never lost it.

cues.zh: 没人夺走过它。
cues.en: No one ever robbed you of that.

cues.zh: 所以，我小时候就是这样学习的；
cues.en: And so, when I was young that's how I was learning;

cues.zh: 我同时学英语和音乐，
cues.en: I was learning English and music at the same time

cues.zh: 而且用的是同样的方式。
cues.en: and in the same way.

cues.zh: 所以我常跟人说：“对，我两三岁就开始打鼓了。”
cues.en: So I tell this to people; I usually say, "Yeah, I started when I was two or three."

cues.zh: 我这么说，只是因为这样更让人信服。
cues.en: And I say that just because that's more believable.

cues.zh: 可你是什么时候开始说英语的？
cues.en: But when did you start speaking English?

cues.zh: 你是等到两三岁才开始说的吗？
cues.en: Did you wait until you were two or three?

cues.zh: 不是。
cues.en: No.

cues.zh: 要我说，你大概出生前就在“说”了。
cues.en: You were speaking, I'd probably say, before birth.

cues.zh: 你能听见声音的时候，大概就已经开始学它了。
cues.en: Whenever you could hear is when you probably started learning it.

cues.zh: 对我来说，这特别特别酷，也特别特别聪明，这是我哥哥们的功劳
cues.en: To me, that's very, very cool, and very very clever of my brothers

cues.zh: ——我大哥，五个兄弟里最大的那个……
cues.en: - my oldest brother, out of the five...

cues.zh: 我是最小的，Reggie是老大——
cues.en: I'm the youngest, Reggie is the oldest -

cues.zh: 他只比我大八岁。
cues.en: He's only eight years older than me.

cues.zh: 所以他怎么会这么聪明，我也不知道。这才是真正的问题。
cues.en: So how he was this smart, I don't know. That's the real question.

cues.zh: 那才该是真正的TED演讲。
cues.en: That should be the real TED talk.

cues.zh: 他是怎么想出这种绝妙办法的
cues.en: How he figured out the ingenious way

cues.zh: 不教我们这些弟弟怎么打鼓！
cues.en: of not teaching us, younger brothers, how to play!

cues.zh: 他一开始根本没把贝斯塞到我手里。
cues.en: He didn't start me by putting a bass in my hands.

cues.zh: No.
cues.en: No.

cues.zh: 他们做的第一件事就是在我周围放音乐
cues.en: The first thing they did was to play music around me

cues.zh: 从我能记事的最早年纪开始。
cues.en: from my earliest age that I can remember.

cues.zh: 我记得住在夏威夷，
cues.en: I can remember living in Hawaii,

cues.zh: 我哥哥们会摆好设备，我记得看到一个塑料凳子。
cues.en: my brothers would set up, and I can remember seeing a plastic stool.

cues.zh: 很多时候我们会在前院摆开
cues.en: A lot of times we'd set up in the front yard

cues.zh: 我能看到一个塑料凳子，
cues.en: where I can see a plastic stool,

cues.zh: 上面放着一个小塑料玩具，米老鼠发条吉他，
cues.en: with a little plastic toy, Mickey Mouse wind-up-guitar,

cues.zh: 就放在那个凳子上。
cues.en: laying on top of that stool.

cues.zh: 没人需要告诉我那是给我的。
cues.en: No one had to tell me that that was for me.

cues.zh: 就像没人需要告诉你什么时候轮到你说话一样。
cues.en: The same way no one has to tell you when it's your turn to talk.

cues.zh: 你知道该怎么做，所以我知道那个凳子是给我的。
cues.en: You know how to do it and so I knew that stool was for me.

cues.zh: 我知道那个乐器是给我的。
cues.en: I knew that instrument was for me.

cues.zh: 上面有塑料琴弦，你上紧发条，它就会播放一首歌。
cues.en: It had plastic strings on it, you would wind it up, and it would play a song.

cues.zh: 但你没法真的靠琴弦来弹奏，重点也不在那。
cues.en: But you couldn't really play it from the strings, and it wasn't about that.

cues.zh: 我长到能拿稳乐器的年纪时，
cues.en: By the time I was old enough to hold an instrument,

cues.zh: 他们给了我个东西握着，纯粹就是为了手里有个东西可握；
cues.en: they gave me something to hold Just for the sake of holding something;

cues.zh: 为往后的岁月做准备。
cues.en: preparing me for the later years.

cues.zh: 重点根本不是演奏那件乐器。
cues.en: It wasn't about playing that instrument.

cues.zh: 这正是我们很多音乐老师犯的错：
cues.en: That's the mistake a lot of us, music teachers make:

cues.zh: 我们先教孩子怎么演奏乐器，可他们还没理解音乐。
cues.en: we teach kids how to play the instrument first, before they understand music.

cues.zh: 你不会教孩子拼写。
cues.en: You don't teach a kid how to spell.

cues.zh: 教孩子拼写“milk”
cues.en: Teaching a kid to spell "milk"

cues.zh: 在他们已经喝了好几年牛奶之前
cues.en: before they've been drinking a lot of it for a few years

cues.zh: 这说不通，对吧？
cues.en: doesn't make sense does it?

cues.zh: 但不知为何，在音乐上我们仍觉得这说得通。
cues.en: But for some reason, we still think it does in music.

cues.zh: 我们想先教他们规则和乐器。
cues.en: We want to teach them the rules and the instruments first.

cues.zh: 但在我大概两岁时，他们把那个玩具放到我手里，
cues.en: But by the time I was about two, and they put that toy in my hands,

cues.zh: 我已经很有音乐感了，因为我相信人生来就懂音乐。
cues.en: I was already very musical because I believe you're born musical.

cues.zh: 听听任何人的声音，听听任何孩子的声音。
cues.en: Just listen to anybody's voice. Listen to any child's voice.

cues.zh: 没有什么音乐比这更纯粹了。
cues.en: There's no purer music than that.

cues.zh: 所以我兄弟们不知怎么就知道我天生有音乐感，
cues.en: So my brothers somehow knew I was born musical,

cues.zh: 但他们想让我当贝斯手，
cues.en: but they wanted me to be a bass player

cues.zh: 所以等我够大了，他们就把玩具塞到我手里，
cues.en: so when I was old enough, they put a toy in my hands,

cues.zh: 然后他们开始演奏。
cues.en: and they would play.

cues.zh: 我就跟着上下蹦跳，也一起拨弦。
cues.en: I would just bounce up and down and strum along, too.

cues.zh: 但最酷的地方还是，这跟乐器无关。
cues.en: But the coolest thing about it, again, is it wasn't about the instrument.

cues.zh: 我学的是玩音乐，不是玩乐器。
cues.en: I was learning to play music not an instrument.

cues.zh: 希望今天我还在延续这一点。
cues.en: And I continue that hopefully today.

cues.zh: 同样，我当时确实知道的是，我明白那意味着什么——
cues.en: Again, what I did know was I knew what it meant

cues.zh: 当我哥哥在四小节乐句结尾打开踩镲的时候。
cues.en: when my brother opened up his high hat at the end of a four-bar phrase.

cues.zh: 或者我学会了这些乐句和那个乐句的对比。
cues.en: Or I learned these phrases versus that phrase.

cues.zh: 就像婴儿知道那意味着什么——
cues.en: The same way a baby knows what it means

cues.zh: 当母亲提高音调的时候，
cues.en: when the mother raises the pitch of her voice

cues.zh: 和父亲降低音调的时候。
cues.en: versus the father lowering the pitch of his.

cues.zh: 你了解这些东西，
cues.en: You know these things,

cues.zh: 哪怕你甚至可能不明白这个词是什么意思。
cues.en: and even though you may not even understand what the word means.

cues.zh: 于是你一直在学习所有这些。
cues.en: And so you're learning all these things.

cues.zh: 等到婴儿能说出一个真正的词时，
cues.en: By the time a baby can speak a real word,

cues.zh: 他们早已对这门语言了解很多了。
cues.en: they know already a lot about the language.

cues.zh: 所以我也是这样学音乐的。
cues.en: So I was learning music the same way.

cues.zh: 等乐器真正拿在手里时，我已经很有音乐感了。
cues.en: By the time I had the instrument in my hands, I was already very musical.

cues.zh: 大概在我三岁左右，
cues.en: When I would turn about three years old,

cues.zh: Reggie把他那把六弦吉他上的两根弦拆了下来。
cues.en: Reggie took two strings off of one of his six-string guitars.

cues.zh: 他拆掉了两根高音弦，那成了我第一件真正的乐器。
cues.en: He took the two high strings off, and that became my first real instrument.

cues.zh: 于是Reggie实际上开始教我
cues.en: So Reggie actually started teaching me

cues.zh: 把手指按在某些位置来弹出音符
cues.en: to put my finger in certain places to produce notes

cues.zh: 弹的是我已经会唱的歌曲。
cues.en: to songs I already knew.

cues.zh: 我不是从零开始。我先有了音乐感。
cues.en: I wasn't starting from the beginning. I was musical first.

cues.zh: 接下来，我只是要把那份音乐通过乐器表达出来。
cues.en: Now, I just had to put that music through an instrument.

cues.zh: 现在回想起来，我意识到我就是这么学会说话的。
cues.en: And looking back on it now, I realize that's how I learned to talk.

cues.zh: 重点从来不在于先学会乐器。
cues.en: It wasn't about learning the instrument first.

cues.zh: 谁在乎你用什么乐器来表达呢？
cues.en: Who cares about the instrument you talk with?

cues.zh: 重要的是你想表达什么。
cues.en: It's about what you have to say.

cues.zh: 在音乐上，我一直保留着自己的声音。
cues.en: I've always musically maintained my own voice.

cues.zh: 我心里总有话想说。
cues.en: I've always had something to say.

cues.zh: 而我也学会了如何通过乐器来表达。
cues.en: And I've learned how to speak through my instrument.

cues.zh: 所以如果我们思考这几点：
cues.en: So if we think about a couple of things

cues.zh: 不用被迫练习，不用别人教你该说什么——
cues.en: not being forced to practice, not being told what you have to say

cues.zh: 我又在拿英语打比方了——不用别人教你该说什么。
cues.en: - I'm speaking English again - not being told what you have to say.

cues.zh: 当老师教你一个英语新单词时，
cues.en: When the teacher teaches you a new word in English,

cues.zh: 她会让你马上把它放进句子里，放到语境中。
cues.en: she has you put it into a sentence; in the context, right away.

cues.zh: 而音乐老师却只会让你回去练习。
cues.en: A music teacher will tell you to go practice it.

cues.zh: 练习确实管用，但远不如直接放进语境里学得快。
cues.en: Practicing works but it's a slower process than putting it into context.

cues.zh: 我们知道的，用英语就是这样。
cues.en: And we know that with English.

cues.zh: 这就是我学习的方式。
cues.en: And so this was the way I learned.

cues.zh: 等我长大一点，大概五岁时，我们其实在巡演；我们五个人。
cues.en: As I grew older, about five years old, we were actually on tour; the five of us.

cues.zh: 我们很幸运能够巡演
cues.en: We were fortunate enough to be able to tour

cues.zh: 为一位伟大的灵魂乐歌手 Curtis Mayfield 做开场。
cues.en: opening for a great soul singer named Curtis Mayfield.

cues.zh: 所以如果我当时五岁，我大哥才只有13岁。
cues.en: So if I was five years old, my oldest brother was only 13.

cues.zh: 但回想起来，我们在那个年纪就能说一口流利的英语。
cues.en: But when I think about it, we could speak good English at that age.

cues.zh: 为什么音乐不行呢？
cues.en: Why not music?

cues.zh: 所以从那时起，我一直把音乐当作一门语言来对待，
cues.en: So I've always, since then, approached music just like a language,

cues.zh: 因为我是在同一时间、以同样的方式学会它的。
cues.en: because I learned it at the same time and in the same way.

cues.zh: 最棒的部分是
cues.en: The best part of it all

cues.zh: 我保留了小孩子与生俱来的某种东西。
cues.en: is I've maintained something that little children are born with.

cues.zh: 那就是自由。
cues.en: And that's freedom.

cues.zh: 我们很多人的音乐自由被说没了，
cues.en: A lot of us are talked out of our musical freedom,

cues.zh: 就在我们第一次上课的时候。
cues.en: when we are first given a lesson.

cues.zh: 因为我们去找老师，
cues.en: Because we go to a teacher,

cues.zh: 而老师很少会去了解我们最初为什么来。
cues.en: and the teacher rarely ever finds out why we came in the first place.

cues.zh: 很多时候，那个弹着空气吉他的孩子
cues.en: A lot of times, that kid playing that air guitar

cues.zh: 那里没有对错之分，
cues.en: where there's no right or wrong,

cues.zh: 不在于音符对不对，也不在于乐器。
cues.en: it's not about the right or wrong notes, it's not about the instrument.

cues.zh: 他们弹奏是因为感觉对了。
cues.en: They're playing because it feels right.

cues.zh: 这和你在淋浴时唱歌的方式和原因是一样的。
cues.en: It's the same way and reason that you sing in the shower.

cues.zh: 或者当你开车上班时，你在唱歌。
cues.en: Or when you're driving to work; you're singing.

cues.zh: 你唱歌不是因为音符正确
cues.en: You're not singing because it's the right notes

cues.zh: 或者你懂正确的音阶，
cues.en: or you know the right scales,

cues.zh: 你唱歌是因为感觉很好。
cues.en: you're singing because it feels good.

cues.zh: 我在早餐时和一位女士聊过，她说，
cues.en: I spoke to a lady at breakfast who said,

cues.zh: “我在淋浴时就是Ella Fitzgerald！”
cues.en: "I'm Ella Fitzgerald when I'm in the shower!"

cues.zh: （笑声）
cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.zh: 当然她说得对！
cues.en: And of course she's right!

cues.zh: 那么为什么当外面有人开始听的时候，这就变了呢？
cues.en: So why does that change when someone outside starts to listen?

cues.zh: 随着我们成长和学习，那种自由就丢失了，
cues.en: That freedom becomes lost as we grow and as we learn,

cues.zh: 我们需要找到一种方法来保持那种自由。
cues.en: and we need to find a way to keep that freedom.

cues.zh: 而且这是可以做到的！
cues.en: And it can be done!

cues.zh: 它并没有永远消失。
cues.en: It's not gone forever.

cues.zh: 一个弹着空气吉他的孩子，脸上会带着笑容。
cues.en: A kid playing air guitar will play with a smile on their face.

cues.zh: 给他们上第一堂课，笑容就消失了。
cues.en: Give them the first lesson, the smile goes away.

cues.zh: 很多时候，你得付出努力
cues.en: A lot of times you have to work for

cues.zh: 用整个音乐生涯，才能把那个笑容找回来。
cues.en: your whole musical life to get that smile back.

cues.zh: 作为老师，我们可以留住那个笑容，只要方法对了。
cues.en: As teachers, we can keep that smile, if we approach it the right way.

cues.zh: 我说的方法，就是把它当作一门语言来教；
cues.en: And I say approach it like a language;

cues.zh: 让学生保持那份自由。
cues.en: allow the student to keep the freedom.

cues.zh: 随着我长大一点，
cues.en: As I got older, a little bit older,

cues.zh: 我和兄弟们开始巡演、频繁演出，
cues.en: and my brothers and I started to tour and play a lot,

cues.zh: 我妈会问一个问题，我一直没真正理解
cues.en: my mom would ask a question that I never understood really

cues.zh: 直到我年长许多、有了自己的孩子。
cues.en: until I got much older and had kids of my own.

cues.zh: 我妈会问我们几个男孩，
cues.en: My Mom would ask us boys,

cues.zh: 她说：“这个世界需要
cues.en: and she was saying, "What does the world need

cues.zh: 再多一个好音乐家吗？”
cues.en: with another good musician?"

cues.zh: 想想这句话。
cues.en: Think about that.

cues.zh: 我说的是音乐，但你可以换成自己的职业。
cues.en: And I'm saying music, but insert your own career.

cues.zh: 这个世界需要你做什么？
cues.en: What does the world need with you?

cues.zh: 这真的让我意识到，随着我年龄的增长，
cues.en: It really made me realize that now, as I've got older,

cues.zh: 音乐不仅仅是一种语言，音乐是一种生活方式。
cues.en: music is more than just a language, music is a lifestyle.

cues.zh: 这就是我的生活方式。
cues.en: It's my lifestyle.

cues.zh: 别误会：我说的不是很多音乐人那种生活方式。
cues.en: Don't get me wrong: I'm not talking about the lifestyle a lot of musicians lead.

cues.zh: 因为我们可以回顾过去的音乐英雄
cues.en: Because we can look back at our musical heroes of the past

cues.zh: 并意识到他们在音乐上取得了巨大成功，
cues.en: and realize that they were huge successes in music,

cues.zh: 但在生活中却同样巨大地失败。
cues.en: but just as huge failures in life.

cues.zh: 我可以举几个例子，但我不想让任何人不高兴；
cues.en: I could name a few of them, but I don't want to upset anybody;

cues.zh: 但如果我们想想我们的英雄，很多人都是那样。
cues.en: but if we think about our heroes, a lot of them were like that.

cues.zh: 我觉得我们的父母当时在为我们准备一些东西
cues.en: I think our parents were preparing us for something

cues.zh: 我们当时不知道，但我觉得她能预见未来。
cues.en: that we didn't know at the time, but I think she could see ahead.

cues.zh: “这个世界需要
cues.en: "What does the world need

cues.zh: 又一个优秀的音乐人吗？”
cues.en: with another good musician?"

cues.zh: 所以我们练习了这么多小时。
cues.en: So we're practicing all these hours.

cues.zh: 我们把整栋房子变成了音乐室
cues.en: We turned our whole house into a music room

cues.zh: 整个社区、全州各地的音乐家都会来
cues.en: where all the neighborhood, all the state-wide musicians would show up.

cues.zh: 我们一起练习，
cues.en: We would practice,

cues.zh: 我父母会花掉他们本没有的钱
cues.en: my parents would spend money they didn't have

cues.zh: 来确保我们能拥有下一件最新的乐器。
cues.en: to make sure we had the next newest instrument.

cues.zh: 每年圣诞节，圣诞老人都会带来最新的东西。
cues.en: Every Christmas, Santa would bring the newest thing.

cues.zh: 那到底是为了什么？
cues.en: What was that about?

cues.zh: 只是为了让我们能赚钱吗？
cues.en: Was it just so that we could make money?

cues.zh: 为了让我们能站在舞台上享受荣耀吗？
cues.en: So that we could stand on stage and bask in the glory?

cues.zh: 我现在意识到，远不止如此。
cues.en: I realize now, that it is much more than that.

cues.zh: 音乐是我的生活方式。
cues.en: Music is my lifestyle.

cues.zh: 而现在，当我真正开始深入学习音乐，
cues.en: And now as I'm going into really studying music,

cues.zh: 以便能以老师的身份与他人分享，
cues.en: so that I could share it with other people in a teacher's role,

cues.zh: 我意识到，我们可以从音乐中学到很多东西
cues.en: I realize that there's a lot that we can learn from music

cues.zh: 并应用到生活中。
cues.en: and apply to our lives.

cues.zh: 要成为一名优秀的音乐家，你必须是一个优秀的倾听者。
cues.en: To be a good musician, you have to be a good listener.

cues.zh: 不管我作为贝斯手有多厉害，或者演奏任何乐器。
cues.en: Doesn't matter how great I am as a bassist, or any instrument.

cues.zh: 不管我有多厉害。
cues.en: Doesn't matter how great I am.

cues.zh: 我们可以把世界上最顶尖的五位音乐家请上这个舞台。
cues.en: We can put five of the world's best musicians on this stage.

cues.zh: 但如果各自为战、互不相顾，
cues.en: But if we're great separate from each other,

cues.zh: 听起来会非常糟糕。
cues.en: it's going to sound horrible.

cues.zh: 但如果我们互相倾听、一起演奏，
cues.en: But if we listen to each other and play together,

cues.zh: 作为个体，我们不必那么出色，
cues.en: individually, we don't have to be as great,

cues.zh: 听起来反而会好得多。
cues.en: and it'll sound much better.

cues.zh: 几年前我连续受邀去加州斯坦福，
cues.en: I was invited a couple years in a row to go to Stanford, in California,

cues.zh: 组建一支音乐团队，给刚入学的新生做演讲。
cues.en: and put together a musical team to address the incoming freshman class.

cues.zh: 我们用音乐让他们感受
cues.en: And we were able to use music to give them an idea

cues.zh: 接下来四年的大学生活可能是什么样。
cues.en: what the next four years of their life might be like.

cues.zh: 用音乐来做这件事很有意思，因为音乐是一种方式，
cues.en: It was fun using music to do it because music is a way

cues.zh: 让我可以谈论任何可能比较敏感的话题：
cues.en: that I can talk about anything that could be kind of touchy:

cues.zh: 政治、种族主义、平等、不平等、宗教。
cues.en: politics, racism, equality, inequality, religion.

cues.zh: 我能通过音乐做到这一点，而且我依然安全。
cues.en: I can do it through music, and I'm still safe.

cues.zh: 我们能从观众中挑一个人
cues.en: We were able to pick someone out of the audience

cues.zh: 这个人以前从未演奏过乐器。
cues.en: who'd never played an instrument before.

cues.zh: 通常是位女性；
cues.en: Usually, it was a female;

cues.zh: 让她上台，我们把贝斯挂在她脖子上，
cues.en: have her come up, we'd strap a bass around her neck,

cues.zh: 然后我让乐队开始演奏。
cues.en: and then I would get the band playing.

cues.zh: 乐队一开始演奏，
cues.en: And as soon as the band starts playing,

cues.zh: 那个人就开始这样做。
cues.en: that person starts doing this.

cues.zh: （笑声）
cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.zh: 我说：“这就是音乐！”
cues.en: And I say, "That's music!"

cues.zh: 如果你听那把贝斯，就像音乐店里的任何乐器一样，
cues.en: If you listen to that bass, like any instrument in a music store,

cues.zh: 它放在那里时，不会发出任何声音。
cues.en: when it's sitting there, it doesn't make a sound.

cues.zh: 所以如果你想让它奏出音乐，你就得把音乐放进去。
cues.en: So if you want music to come out of that, you have to put it there.

cues.zh: 而你脖子里的那种律动，你只需要把它放进乐器里。
cues.en: And that groove that's in your neck, you just have to put it in the instrument.

cues.zh: 所以我 just 让她用左手捏住琴颈
cues.en: So I just had her with her left hand squeeze the neck

cues.zh: - 因为每个人都知道怎么拿乐器，这并不新鲜 -
cues.en: - because everyone knows how to hold an instrument, that's not new -

cues.zh: 捏住它，然后让你的右手在琴弦上舞动。
cues.en: squeeze it and then, let your right hand dance, on the string.

cues.zh: 她跟着那个音符开始摇摆，乐队在她周围奏起来。
cues.en: She starts bouncing on that note, and the band kicks up around her.

cues.zh: 突然间，她就成了贝斯手。
cues.en: All of a sudden, she's a bassist.

cues.zh: 更进一步说，她成了音乐人。
cues.en: More so, she's a musician.

cues.zh: 舞者跳舞前从不需要问问题。
cues.en: A dancer never has to ask questions before they dance.

cues.zh: 歌手通常不用问我们是什么调。
cues.en: A singer doesn't usually have to ask what key are we in.

cues.zh: 音乐人却要问太多问题。
cues.en: Musicians have to ask too many questions.

cues.zh: 所以这教会我的是：“哇！
cues.en: So what that taught me is that, "Wow!

cues.zh: 因为我们很厉害，她什么都不用懂。”
cues.en: Because we're great, she doesn't have to know anything."

cues.zh: （笑声）
cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.zh: 突然间，任何人走进房间看到这支乐队
cues.en: And all of a sudden, anyone who were to walk into the room and see this band

cues.zh: 台上有个新来的，
cues.en: with this newcomer on stage,

cues.zh: 没人分得清谁是新人。
cues.en: no one would know who was the newcomer.

cues.zh: 这让我明白：“哇！
cues.en: So that let me know, "Wow!

cues.zh: 如果我把自己的厉害用对地方，就能帮别人快速成长起来。”
cues.en: If I use my greatness in the right way, it can help others rise up quickly."

cues.zh: 而斯坦福那整件事最酷的地方
cues.en: And the coolest thing about that whole thing in Stanford

cues.zh: 是她能把贝斯带回家！
cues.en: is she got to take the bass home!

cues.zh: （笑声）
cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.zh: 我最近见过她，她还是个贝斯手
cues.en: I saw her recently, she is still a bassist

cues.zh: 所以那很棒。
cues.en: so that's great.

cues.zh: 倾听是我们可以用于生活的绝佳音乐关键，
cues.en: Listening is a great musical key that we can use for life,

cues.zh: 当然，合作也是帮助他人变得出色的绝佳方式。
cues.en: working together, of course, being great to help other people become great.

cues.zh: 当人们把你捧上神坛时，
cues.en: When people put you up on a pedestal,

cues.zh: 不要走下神坛装作谦逊。
cues.en: don't come off the pedestal acting like you're humble.

cues.zh: 就留在那神坛上，
cues.en: Stay up on that pedestal,

cues.zh: 因为如果他们把你捧上去，那是在向你展示他们能看多高。
cues.en: because if they put you there that's showing you how high they can see.

cues.zh: 留在那里，把他们也拉上来。
cues.en: Stay there and pull them up.

cues.zh: 他们会比你走下来时成长得更快。
cues.en: And they'll grow faster than if you come down.

cues.zh: 所以我们要帮助这些人，因为我们很出色。
cues.en: So we're going to help these people because we're great.

cues.zh: 在音乐里，通常，除非你说我很棒，否则我并不棒。
cues.en: In music, usually, I'm not great until you say I am, anyway.

cues.zh: 他们说：“他赢了所有这些格莱美奖。”
cues.en: They say, "He's won all these Grammy's."

cues.zh: 没有你们大家，我什么都赢不了。
cues.en: I can't win anything without you all.

cues.zh: 我妈妈总是教我们的另一件事
cues.en: Another thing my mom always taught us

cues.zh: 是：“孩子们，你们已经成功了。
cues.en: is, "You boys are already successful.

cues.zh: 世界其他地方只是还不知道而已！”
cues.en: The rest of the world just doesn't know it yet!"

cues.zh: 当时我不明白，但现在我真的真的懂了。
cues.en: I didn't understand that then, but I really, really do now.

cues.zh: 很快，在我离开之前，我想让你们思考一下这个：
cues.en: Really quickly, before I get out of here I just want you to think about this:

cues.zh: 如果我要弹两个音，比如说我弹一个C；
cues.en: If I were to play two notes, Let's say I play a C;

cues.zh: ——只需要你们发挥想象力——
cues.en: - just want you to use your imagination -

cues.zh: 如果我弹一个C和一个紧挨着的升C，
cues.en: if I play a C and a C-sharp right next to each other,

cues.zh: 听起来大概会觉得这两个音冲突；
cues.en: it'll probably sound like those notes clash;

cues.zh: “错了！”“难听！”
cues.en: "Wrong!", "Bad!"

cues.zh: 但如果我把C升高一个八度，
cues.en: But if I take the C up an octave,

cues.zh: 再弹升C和C。
cues.en: play the C-sharp and the C again.

cues.zh: 突然间，听起来就很美了。
cues.en: All of a sudden, it sounds beautiful.

cues.zh: 同样的两个音。
cues.en: Same two notes.

cues.zh: 那个C变成了升C的大七度
cues.en: That C becomes a major seventh to the C-sharp

cues.zh: 这是让一个和弦美得几乎过分、好听至极的关键要素。
cues.en: which is a key element that makes a chord almost too beautiful, too nice sounding.

cues.zh: 那么，同样的两个音，怎么会在一种情况下听起来冲突难听
cues.en: So how can the same two notes sound bad and clash in one instance

cues.zh: 而在另一种情况下却很美呢？
cues.en: and beautiful in another?

cues.zh: 把它带进生活里。
cues.en: Just take that to life.

cues.zh: 当我们在生活中看到糟糕、可怕或恐怖的事情时，
cues.en: When we see something bad, or awful, or horrible in life,

cues.zh: 也许我们只是用错了音区来看待它。
cues.en: maybe we're just reviewing it in the wrong octave.

cues.zh: 也许我们可以换个视角。
cues.en: Maybe we could change our perspective.

cues.zh: 其实，如果你看到什么不对劲的事，
cues.en: Actually, if you see something that's wrong,

cues.zh: 你该知道，你是用错了音区在看它
cues.en: you should know that you're seeing it in the wrong octave

cues.zh: 然后想办法改变你的视角。
cues.en: and find a way to change your viewpoint.

cues.zh: 或者用音乐术语来说——换个音区。
cues.en: Or to use a musical term - change your octave.

cues.zh: 各国制造炸弹，目的是伤害人、
cues.en: Countries make bombs with the goal of hurting people,

cues.zh: 制造恐惧、杀人、证明立场。
cues.en: instilling fear, killing people, proving a point.

cues.zh: 国家、政府在炸弹送出前为其祈福。
cues.en: Countries, governments bless the bombs before they're sent.

cues.zh: 这是自上而下发生的，从政府往下。
cues.en: This happens from the top-down, the government down.

cues.zh: 这就是我们的答案。
cues.en: This is our answer.

cues.zh: 这让我意识到，解决方案可能得自下而上产生。
cues.en: Makes me realize that the solution may have to come from the bottom-up.

cues.zh: 有人在研发一种让人爱上你的炸弹吗？
cues.en: Is anyone working on a bomb that makes people love you?

cues.zh: 也许是一颗丘比特炸弹？
cues.en: Maybe a cupid bomb?

cues.zh: 我相信我们早就拥有它了。
cues.en: I believe we already have it.

cues.zh: 它就是音乐。
cues.en: It's called Music.

cues.zh: 每个国家都有属于自己的版本。
cues.en: And every country has their own version of it.

cues.zh: 而且它确实管用，它能把人们凝聚在一起。
cues.en: And it works. It brings people together.

cues.zh: 你就算一窍不通，也能心领神会。
cues.en: You don't have to know a thing about it to get it.

cues.zh: 它是一种语言，是一种生活方式。
cues.en: It's a language. It's a lifestyle.

cues.zh: 它能拯救世界。
cues.en: And it can save the world.

cues.zh: 我叫 Victor Wooten，是一名音乐人。
cues.en: My name is Victor Wooten. I'm a musician.

cues.zh: 希望大家能和我一起奔赴这个“战场”。
cues.en: And I hope you'll join me on the battlefield.

cues.zh: （笑声）
cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.zh: 谢谢大家。
cues.en: Thank you.

cues.zh: （掌声）
cues.en: (Applause)
